A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NOICE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title, organization, and layout.

before.justification: V3 reports original attack evaluations on open-source models, GPT-4o, and Claude Haiku, including defense comparisons, scaling experiments, and generated-output examples.

after.justification: V4 retains those original empirical results and adds an evaluation against constrained training in Table 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Table 9 retain the same NOICE construction, including the Gemma adaptation. AMD still generates an initial prefix with an aligned model. V4's expanded, stepwise explanation does not establish a changed attack procedure.

E1.justification: Both use HelpSteer-derived training data, LLM-LAT/harmful-dataset, and the 300-prompt HeX-PHI evaluation. The new constrained-training experiment retains the existing harmful-request task and data coverage.

E2.justification: V4 evaluates Qi et al. (2024a)'s constrained-training defense in Table 6. FRD disappears from the main cross-model and model-size comparisons, although selected FRD comparisons remain in Tables 16–17. YOC is renamed Implicit without changing its implementation.

E3.justification: V4 Table 6 introduces constrained optimization on the first five tokens for Llama-3-8B-Instruct. The GPT-4o sample-output caption changes from 5000 to 1000 training examples (v3 Table 7; v4 Table 5), aligning with the 1000-example protocol already stated in v3; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 6 tests whether NOICE withstands training-time constraints on initial tokens. Some FRD robustness evidence, including Mistral and model-size sweep results, is removed. The training-size analyses in Tables 16–17 and the appendix case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use ± values and shaded uncertainty bands. V4 adds no run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, or significance-testing procedures; its new Table 6 follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 Table 6 adds constrained-training ASRs of 0.59 for NOICE, 0.06 for Vanilla SFT, 0.07 for ISA, and 0.24 for Implicit. Some FRD entries disappear, including Mistral and model-size results. Matched retained scores, including GPT-4o's 57%, Claude's 72%, and Tables 16–17, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 revises the explicit attacker-resource assumption from at most 5000 sequences of at most 1000 tokens to a $100 API-credit budget. The mathematical probability decomposition remains unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central shallow-attack/deeper-NOICE claims and headline 57%/72% ASRs remain. V4 drops the abstract's claimed average 3.25-fold advantage on defended open-source models and introduces a sevenfold GPT-4o superiority claim in the introduction. That new ratio does not follow from Table 3's 0.57 versus the best prior attack's 0.06.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the constrained-training result as additional evidence of attack depth. Section 3.3 also strengthens AMD's comparison with LG from comparable protection to superiority for Implicit and ISA, although Table 8 shows exceptions: Llama ISA ASR is 0.14 under AMD versus 0.11 under LG. FRD's oracle limitations are omitted.

D1.justification: New Appendix F discloses A100 allocations and approximate training and sampling times. Section 3.2 documents how the existing conditional probabilities were measured using prefixes and GPT judging. Conversely, v3's AMD prefix length of 15 tokens and FRD definition disappear, despite retained FRD appendix results.

R1.justification: V4 adds Davies et al. (2025), removes Leong et al. (2024), and links the renamed Implicit attack to the already-cited Li et al. (2025b). Most research positioning remains; the older data-poisoning discussion moves to Appendix E.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and mechanism exposition are extensively rewritten around shallow versus deeper attacks. The probabilistic framework now precedes NOICE, production results come first, and baseline details and older related work move into appendices. The title, author block, and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the two-column main text with a single-column layout, redraws the dataset-generation diagram, relocates the probability schematic, removes v3 Figure 3, merges model-size tables, and adds Table 6. Several plots and tables lose FRD panels or columns, while Tables 16–17 retain FRD results.

improvement.justification: The new constrained-training comparison tests the central attack-depth claim against a previously unevaluated type of defense. Clearer organization, probability-measurement explanations, and compute disclosures also improve assessability. These provide a limited net gain, tempered by missing AMD/FRD reproduction details and new comparative overstatements. Most underlying empirical evidence remains unchanged.
